questions.stem:
Statement: Exercise daily to stay healthy.
Conclusion I: People who exercise daily tend to be healthier.
Conclusion II: Only people who exercise daily can be healthy.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: A is correct. I follows logically from the statement. II adds 'only' — an absolute restriction not stated. II doesn't follow.

questions.stem:
Statement: The company's profits have decreased for the third consecutive quarter.
Conclusion I: The company is facing financial difficulties.
Conclusion II: The company should immediately lay off all employees.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: A is correct. I logically follows — three consecutive quarters of declining profit indicates financial strain. II recommends a drastic action not suggested by the statement alone.

questions.stem:
Statement: Smoking causes cancer and heart disease.
Conclusion I: Non-smokers never get cancer or heart disease.
Conclusion II: Smoking should be discouraged to reduce cancer rates.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II follows — if smoking causes cancer, discouraging it should reduce cancer rates. I uses 'never' — the statement doesn't say cancer is caused ONLY by smoking; other causes exist. I is too absolute.

questions.stem:
Statement: Many students fail in mathematics due to lack of practice.
Conclusion I: Regular practice can help students pass mathematics.
Conclusion II: All students who practice mathematics will pass.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: A is correct. I logically follows — if lack of practice causes failure, practice should help. II uses 'all' — too absolute and not supported by the statement.

questions.stem:
Statement: Reading is the best way to improve vocabulary.
Conclusion I: People who read extensively have a good vocabulary.
Conclusion II: One cannot improve vocabulary without reading.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: A is correct. I follows from the statement. II implies reading is the ONLY way — but 'best way' allows other ways to exist. II is too restrictive.

questions.stem:
Statement: A bridge in the city collapsed due to poor construction quality.
Conclusion I: All bridges in the city are unsafe.
Conclusion II: Strict quality checks should be imposed on construction projects.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II follows as a logical preventive measure. I over-generalises from one bridge to 'all bridges' — an unwarranted conclusion.

questions.stem:
Statement: Vegetables are essential for a balanced diet.
Conclusion I: A person who does not eat vegetables cannot be healthy.
Conclusion II: A balanced diet must include vegetables.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II follows directly (statement says vegetables are essential for a balanced diet = a balanced diet must include them). I says 'cannot be healthy' — that is too strong; people can manage health in other ways. I doesn't follow.

questions.stem:
Statement: Mobile internet has transformed the way people consume news.
Conclusion I: Traditional newspapers are no longer popular.
Conclusion II: More people now access news through the internet than before.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II is a reasonable inference — if mobile internet transformed news consumption, internet news access has grown. I says newspapers are 'no longer popular' — 'transformed' doesn't imply newspapers are dead; I is too extreme.

questions.stem:
Statements: (I) All children like chocolate. (II) Some adults like chocolate.
Conclusion I: Some adults are children.
Conclusion II: Some people who like chocolate are children.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II: All children like chocolate means children are a subset of chocolate-likers → some chocolate-likers are children ✓. I: Adults and children both liking chocolate gives no basis to say some adults ARE children — liking the same thing doesn't make them the same group. I doesn't follow.

questions.stem:
Statement: Despite a record cold wave, energy-efficient buildings in the northern district consumed 30% less heating fuel than conventional ones.
Conclusion I: Energy-efficient buildings are completely unaffected by extreme cold.
Conclusion II: Adopting energy-efficient designs can substantially reduce fuel consumption even in extreme weather.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: B is correct. II follows directly — 30% less fuel 'even during a record cold wave' supports that energy-efficient designs reduce consumption in extreme conditions. I uses 'completely unaffected' — the buildings still consumed fuel (just 30% less), so they were affected; I is too extreme.
